card.title: N1K1 KYOFU
card.text: Deployment: Shuffle a IJN MIKURA into your deck.
card.flavorText: The Kawanishi N1K1 Kyōfū, given the Allied reporting name “Rex”), was a floatplane fighter designed for Imperial Japanese Navy operations carried from locations without airstrips. Developed to support Japan’s early-war offensives, it entered service in 1943, by which time Japan had shifted to the defensive. Performance demands from the Navy were highly ambitious for a floatplane, and the Kyōfū fell short. Powered by a Mitsubishi MK4C Kasei 13 engine, it had a top speed of 489 km/h, well below the Navy’s 574 km/h requirement. The aircraft featured a large central float and two stabilizing wing-mounted floats, which added drag and reduced maneuverability. Armed with a heavy cannon and machine guns, it nonetheless struggled against faster US fighters. Only a small number were deployed, operating from Ambon, the Aru Islands and Penang. Kyōfūs also took part in the defense of Okinawa and flew late-war homeland defense missions from Lake Biwa under the Sasebo and Ōtsu Air Corps. Though it saw limited success in combat, its basic design led to the creation of the land-based N1K-J Shiden, a more effective fighter that shed the float and ultimately became one of Japan’s best late-war aircraft.
